secrets.storage/authored/a-custody-failu.purpose: A custody service that cannot reach its database makes a write, read, delete and listing unavailable, and the secret survives.

secrets.storage/authored/a-keychain-faul.purpose: A keychain that fails a write, a read or a delete answers unavailable, stores nothing and removes nothing.

secrets.storage/authored/a-keychain-secr.purpose: A secret written to the keychain is replaced, read, listed, renamed and deleted, and is gone afterwards.

secrets.storage/authored/a-name-in-a-nam.purpose: Every secret command in a namespace that does not exist, or no longer does, is unresolved and reaches no backend.

secrets.storage/authored/a-name-of-128-b.purpose: A name of exactly 128 bytes with a 64-byte segment is accepted, so an oversized value is refused as too large rather than the name.

secrets.storage/authored/a-name-of-129-b.purpose: A name of 129 bytes whose segments are each 64 bytes is refused as too long and stores nothing.

secrets.storage/authored/a-namespace-on-.purpose: A namespace mounted on the remote backend takes a put, a replace, a listing, a rename and a delete through the CLI.

secrets.storage/authored/a-new-name-of-1.purpose: A rename to a name of 129 bytes is refused as a new name that is too long and renames nothing.

secrets.storage/authored/a-remote-secret.purpose: A namespace mounted on the custody service stores, replaces, reads, lists, renames and deletes a secret.

secrets.storage/authored/a-second-tenant.purpose: Every storage command in tenant acme is denied, even with a name the port would refuse, and nothing is stored.

secrets.storage/authored/a-second-user-i.purpose: Every storage command for user alice in tenant default is denied, even with a name the port would refuse.

secrets.storage/authored/a-segment-of-65.purpose: A name with one 65-byte segment is refused as an invalid name although its total is within 128 bytes.

secrets.storage/authored/a-value-above-o.purpose: A value one byte larger than 1 MiB is refused as too large and stores nothing.

secrets.storage/authored/a-value-the-cus.purpose: A 1 MiB value, within the port's bound, is too large for a namespace on the custody service and stores nothing.

secrets.storage/authored/a-value-written.purpose: A value written to the keychain, and the value that replaces it, each read back byte for byte.
A value written through the custody service, and the value that replaces it, each read back byte for byte.

secrets.storage/authored/bind-binds-a-na.purpose: Bind binds a name to a locator, binding it again is a conflict, a bound name cannot be renamed, and a missing namespace is not-found.

secrets.storage/authored/changes-on-a-re.purpose: A write, a delete, a rename and a listing on a read-only mount are unsupported and reach no backend.

secrets.storage/authored/conflicts-the-s.purpose: Adding an existing namespace, moving or removing one that holds secrets, binding twice, renaming a bound name and renaming onto a stored name are conflicts.

secrets.storage/authored/delete-removes-.purpose: Delete removes a secret, and deleting it again is not-found.

secrets.storage/authored/describe-shows-.purpose: Describe shows a secret's name, scope and version, the same row the listing holds, in any namespace.

secrets.storage/authored/each-namespace-.purpose: Each namespace reaches only the backend it is mounted on, and after SetMount only the new one.

secrets.storage/authored/list-reads-the-.purpose: List reads the names of a namespace's secrets, and each namespace's secrets stay in it.

secrets.storage/authored/mount-set-moves.purpose: Mount set moves an empty namespace to a configured backend, and refuses an unconfigured one and a namespace that holds secrets.

secrets.storage/authored/namespace-add-c.purpose: Namespace add creates a namespace on the default mount or the one named, and adding it again is a conflict.

secrets.storage/authored/namespace-list-.purpose: Namespace list holds namespace default and every added namespace, each with its mount.

secrets.storage/authored/namespace-remov.purpose: Namespace remove removes an empty namespace, and refuses namespace default and a namespace that holds a secret.

secrets.storage/authored/put-stores-a-se.purpose: Put stores a value under a name in tenant and user default, and a second put of the name replaces it.

secrets.storage/authored/rename-moves-a-.purpose: Rename moves a secret to a new name in its namespace, and the old name holds nothing afterwards.

secrets.storage/authored/tenant-and-user.purpose: The local user runs every storage command to success in a namespace of its own.

secrets.storage/authored/the-same-name-i.purpose: One name written in two namespaces on the same keychain is two secrets, and deleting one leaves the other.
One name written in two namespaces on the custody service is two secrets, and deleting one leaves the other.

secrets.storage/authored/unbind-removes-.purpose: Unbind removes a name's binding, unbinding it again is not-found, and the name can then be renamed.
